title: The volume control via hotkeys doesn’t work in Chromium and Firefox
line: The Media volume shortcuts no longer show a moving volume indicator for Chrome, which ignores the change, and the indicator now shows the volume players really apply.
explanation: The Media Controller's volume shortcuts set the active player's MPRIS Volume and showed the OSD as soon as the D-Bus call succeeded, also writing the requested value into the player's volume. Chrome/Chromium accept the call but ignore it (their Properties.Set is a no-op that returns success, and Volume always stays 1.0), so the OSD moved and drifted further with each press while the sound stayed the same. Now the OSD is shown only when the player reports the new volume through PropertiesChanged, and the player's volume is only ever what it reports; quick successive presses continue from the last requested value until the player has reported each change.

commits.message:
libkmpris: Show the volume OSD once the player applies the change

Chromium accepts setting its MPRIS Volume but ignores it, so the media
volume shortcuts moved the OSD while the volume stayed the same. Show
the OSD from the volume the player reports, and keep only that value.

CCBUG: 526656

media.caption: Master: five presses of Media volume down with Chrome playing at 30%; the OSD moves down to 75% but Chrome's volume doesn't change.
Fixed: the same five presses show no OSD, since Chrome doesn't apply them.
Master after the presses: OSD says 75%, Chrome still at 30% (its MPRIS Volume still 1).
Fixed after the presses: no misleading OSD.

review.text: The patch only uses CCBUG: 526656 and does not fix the reported problem (media volume shortcuts still fail to change Chromium's volume, and Firefox was not tested); hiding a misleading OSD is reasonable in libkmpris, but the PlayerContainer state machine has concrete bugs. Counting m_volumeChangesPending 1-to-1 between Set calls and PropertiesChanged emissions leaks whenever a player ignores Set without error or coalesces rapid Set calls into fewer signals, leaving m_volumeOSDPending stuck true (spurious OSDs on later in-app volume changes) and causing volume jumps from stale m_requestedVolume; additionally, pressing Volume Up first on Chrome (stuck at Volume 1.0) still hits the boundary branch and shows a fake 100% OSD.
changes: Fix the PlayerContainer volume-tracking state machine so it does not rely on a 1-to-1 count between D-Bus Set calls and PropertiesChanged signals (coalesced PropertiesChanged emissions or players ignoring Set without error permanently leak m_volumeChangesPending, causing stale m_requestedVolume jumps and spurious OSD popups on later in-app volume changes).
Prevent showing a misleading 100% OSD when pressing Media Volume Up on a player like Chromium whose MPRIS Volume is permanently 1.0 and m_volumeChangesPending is 0.

Investigate and test the Firefox part of Bug 526656 as well, and ensure Bug 526656 is actually resolved (either via a complete Plasma-side fix with a BUG: 526656 commit in the appropriate layer such as plasma-pa / plasma-browser-integration, or by tracking this strictly as a standalone libkmpris OSD improvement while handling the upstream browser bugs separately rather than marking 526656 fixed with only CCBUG:).

reviews.text: The commit only has CCBUG and, by its own notes, the media volume shortcuts still don't change Chrome's volume and Firefox's jump to 100% isn't addressed. It only removes the misleading OSD, so the bug ('volume control via hotkeys doesn't work in Chromium and Firefox', which the reporter says used to work) isn't closed. The rig used a plain Chrome with no Plasma Browser Integration, but PBI's MPRIS player implements Volume and libkmpris filters the native Chrome player out by KDEPid, so the regression the reporter describes was never investigated in their likely setup. The new pending counter also has a hazard: a player that merges several Sets into one PropertiesChanged, or never reports one, leaves m_volumeChangesPending above zero for good. Then later app-side volume changes pop the OSD, and presses keep starting from a stale m_requestedVolume.
changes: Reproduce with Plasma Browser Integration installed in Chrome/Chromium and Firefox, find what regressed (which player the Media Controller targets, PBI's Volume handling, or the duplicate filter), and fix it so the shortcuts really change the browser's volume; then use BUG: 526656
Fix or explain the Firefox jump to 100% (player reporting 1.0 while the page is at 30%) as part of the same change, or show it is gone

Make the pending state self-healing: clear m_volumeChangesPending/m_volumeOSDPending when the reported Volume equals m_requestedVolume or after a short timeout, so merged or missing PropertiesChanged signals can't leave it stuck

Without PBI, if Chrome's native MPRIS really can't set Volume, either fall back to the stream volume in the proper layer (plasma-pa) or show why the bug can only close upstream, with the Chromium report filed and linked
